messages:
maria: Heads up — after the kernel fallback change rolled yesterday we see a clear p99 tail regression on /generate. p95 ~ 72ms (ok) but p99 jumped from 240ms -> 520ms during our evening spike. config: max_batch_tokens=8192, max_wait_ms=8. KV cache hit rate dropped ~6% at tail.

jin: thanks — is the traffic distribution same as before? any change in request length mix/seq len?

maria: no deploys to models other than the kernel fallback; sequence length distribution is identical. QPS peaked ~1850, avg seq len ~220. tail correlates with short bursts of 10-50 reqs.

sam: I ran a quick profile on a repro trace. top lines:
```
GPU kernel times (ms): matmul 1.2, attn_fast 0.9, fallback_attn 3.6
KV cache: hit_rate=0.81 overall, tail window hit_rate=0.75
scheduler: queue_delay_p95=6.8ms, queue_delay_p99=52ms
```
Looks like when fallback_attn engages we pay ~3x kernel time and requests pile up -> higher queue_delay_p99.

olivia: interesting — that suggests kernel selection has non-linear impact on queueing. two levers: lower max_wait_ms so fewer requests wait and force smaller microbatches, or reduce max_batch_tokens to limit how big a batch can get when fallback is active.

maria: I tried a quick canary: set max_wait_ms=4 on 10% of traffic and left max_batch_tokens at 8192. results: p95 ~74ms, p99 ~380ms (improved but still above baseline). tail KV hit rate slightly better (0.77).

sam: can you paste the exact patch you applied?

maria: sure — patch applied via rolling config:
```
PATCH /api/v1/scheduler/config
{
  "selector": "model:*",
  "patch": {
    "max_wait_ms": 4
  }
}
```
Applied at 18:42 UTC.

jin: what if we do the opposite: keep max_wait_ms=8 but drop max_batch_tokens to 4096 so batches complete faster when fallback kernels are present? that could reduce p99 without increasing scheduling churn.

olivia: plus consider per-model dynamic thresholds: models that hit fallback frequently get stricter max_wait_ms. We can update routing policy to mark a model as "fallback-hot" when fallback_rate > 2% and automatically reduce max_wait_ms to 3ms and max_batch_tokens to 4096.

sam: quick synthetic run for the 4096 change (10% traffic): p95 75ms, p99 290ms, queue_delay_p99 28ms, kv_tail_hit 0.79. So that looks better than just lowering max_wait.

perf-bot: perf-alert: service=/generate p99 regression -> 520ms -> mitigated to 290ms on canary with max_batch_tokens=4096; tags: auto-bisect=none.

maria: promising. tradeoffs: throughput dropped ~2.3% on the canary and GPU utilization lower by ~4%. but for customers with tight latency SLOs we prefer this.

olivia: action items: (1) run 1h A/B at 50% with max_batch_tokens=4096 + fallback-hot dynamic rule, (2) add kernel-cost tag to profiler so scheduler can pick kernels proactively when it predicts fallback, (3) add a short jitter to max_wait_ms (uniform -1..+2ms) to avoid synchronized batching spikes.

jin: I'll own the A/B and metric dashboard (p95/p99, queue_delay, kv_hit). sam, can you add the kernel-cost tag to the profiler? maria, can you coordinate rollout windows and rollback plan?

maria: yep — starting the A/B at 20:10 UTC. rollback ready if p99 > 350ms for 10 consecutive mins. :thumbsup:

sam: noted, I'll have a PR for kernel-cost tags in the profiler today.

olivia: also worth logging microbatch size distribution per-request so we can see if smaller microbatches correlate with lower tail when fallback happens.

maria: adding that to the rollout checklist. thanks all.
